restrictions: Target sha256-r37-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..36 on every padded block, standard IV once, FIPS padding, full feed-forward, all eight digest words. The collision is ordinary: two distinct 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' sharing their first block; the padding block is identical.

The algorithm is the 37-step collision attack of ePrint 2026/1120 (Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian, Zhu; Section 4.2, "Application to 37-step SHA-2") on its published characteristic (Table 15, relations Table 16), with the words of its published one-block SFS pair (Table 17) used as the Step-1 words of our second block. Every phase is charged. The Step-1 words are nonuniform advice, not a free input: the authors' search that produced them (characteristic and whole SFS pair) is charged by an allowance of 2^70 units, and a fresh Step-1 run at 4 x the paper's Step-1 cost on its own line. No collision of the target is used; the SFS pair's chaining value is not the IV. No certificate is attached and no collision is claimed to have been found.

Time: N = 2^78.51 first-block trials at 1 target compression plus 128 counted ops each; valid first blocks (cap 1.02 N 2^-10) at 2048 ops; Step-3 continuations under a hard cap at 8192 ops; verification; the advice allowance; a voluntary fresh Step-1 overcharge; enumeration. Total 2^78.5830 units, claim 78.59.

Success >= 0.39 with every measured count at an exact one-sided Poisson bound (Bonferroni-split, jointly >= 95%): q2 >= 2^-10.002 (2,097,970 of 2,147,483,648 independent uniform first blocks valid), |S| = 32 (exact), and G >= 2^-69.513, the probability that Step 3 succeeds on a valid first block (product of pooled per-step pass rates, H5). An organizer experiment re-measures q2 and the step-16 conditions at sandbox scale.
Memory is a reported metric only: below 2^16 bytes; nonuniform data (characteristic tables, Step-1 words, round constants) 2,892 bytes.

heuristics.statement: The 37-step characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 (Table 15) with its relations (Table 16), read as stated in proof.md Section 2, and the second-block words of its SFS pair (Table 17) define a valid Step-1 solution and the conditions of the attack.
heuristics.scope: The characteristic, the relations and the 30 Step-1 words. The Step-1 words are nonuniform advice produced by the authors' SFS search, charged by the H4 allowance (and a fresh Step-1 run on its own line); they are not a free input. Every output shares W8..W13 with the published SFS pair, and W14, W15 come from S, which contains the pair's own; the pair's chaining value and W0..W7 are never used. The SFS pair is not a collision of the target (its chaining value is not the IV), and no collision of the target is used. The first block, the chaining value, the Step-3 choices and the collision are computed and charged by the algorithm.
heuristics.limitations: One printed relation needs a reading: orientation: A16[29] = A17[29] holds on the primed message (a differing bit); on the unprimed one it reads A16[29] != A17[29]. The transcription is checked against the paper's own pair, not against an independent source.
heuristics.extrapolation: Every symbol of all 41 rows and every relation as used holds on the paper's SFS pair; the stage measurement produced 272 further 37-step pairs that follow the characteristic and collide under their own chaining values; the per-step pass rates of steps 16..22 match the printed condition counts within 0.02 bit.

heuristics.statement: The Step-3 measurement model (W0..W7 uniform given the Step-2 conditions, which is exactly the attack's distribution when CV1 is uniform, since CV1 maps one-to-one onto W0..W7 for fixed Step-1 words) gives the attack's pass rates: CV1 = f(IV, M0) for independent uniform first blocks M0 behaves as uniform for the conditions of steps 16 onward. With q2 >= 2^-10.002 and G >= 2^-69.513 a first-block trial succeeds with probability >= 2^-79.515; first blocks are independent uniform draws (fresh random words), so N = 2^78.51 trials succeed with probability >= 0.3923.
heuristics.scope: The success probability of the stated N; not the time bound, which holds on every coin sequence under the hard caps.
heuristics.limitations: The uniformity of CV1 for these conditions is a premise; it is tested on real first blocks only up to step 16 (natural Step-3 run and the organizer experiment). The rates themselves carry exact Bonferroni-split Poisson bounds.
heuristics.extrapolation: The natural Step-3 run on real first blocks (run37.txt) gives the step-16 rate 2^-17.00 (511 of 67050784 pairs) against the model's pooled 2^-17.014, and every step-16 relation has the marginal rate 2^-1.000 there. The pooled per-step rates match the printed counts. The organizer experiment re-measures q2 and the step-16 conditions on independent first blocks with pre-registered intervals.

heuristics.statement: The probability that steps 16..36 pass is at least the product of the pooled per-step pass rates of the stage run (2^-74.151; exact joint lower bound 2^-74.467), each rate taken over the states that passed the earlier steps, one continuation per state.
heuristics.scope: P, hence G and the success probability.
heuristics.limitations: Pooling weights each surviving state equally rather than by its pass probability, so the product is not exactly unbiased if pass rates correlate across steps. The draw-level Poisson bounds treat draws at one state as independent; the cluster-level check over starts (proof.md Section 6) supports the same bound. Steps after 17 are measured only on the stage model, not on real first blocks.
heuristics.extrapolation: The unbiased per-start estimator of the same runs (each start's product of pass fractions times its exact collision indicator) gives 2^-73.961, 0.19 bit above the pooled product, so the pooled product is the lower of the two. Every pooled step rate matches its printed condition count (proof.md Section 2).

heuristics.statement: Each first-block trial is one call of the target compression (1 unit) plus at most 128 primitive word operations; each valid first block adds at most 2048; each Step-3 continuation at most 8192.
heuristics.scope: The ordinary-operation terms of the ledger.
heuristics.limitations: The bounds are counted from the pseudocode of proof.md Section 5, not from a compiled program.
heuristics.extrapolation: Doubling every charged operation bound (128, 2048 and 8192) adds 0.066 bit to the total.

heuristics.statement: The authors' search for the characteristic and for the SFS pair that supplies the Step-1 words (nonuniform advice) costs at most 2^70 units.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing term of the ledger.
heuristics.limitations: The paper does not report the search time; the allowance is not a measurement. The rounded claim holds while the allowance is at most 2^71.51 units.
heuristics.extrapolation: The comparable four-step search for the CRYPTO 2026 35-step characteristic was measured at 593,858 CPU-s (x32 for blind re-derivation, 2^45.9 units) in the promoted r32 package; the paper's Table 1 lists SFS collisions at 38 and 39 steps (earlier works) as practical, and the paper prints its own SFS pair at this step count. 2^70 units is about 2^24 times the r32 figure. An allowance of 2^74 would give 2^78.6384.
